hypothesis: Test whether allowing slow local reasoning generation to finish removes the observed transport timeout and permits autonomous resource acquisition and completed productive work during longer uninterrupted play. All gameplay instructions, model weights, sampling, output tokens, context bounds, dispatch budget and periodic checkpoints remain unchanged from long-v1.
notes: Begin every new native campaign from the original digest-bound save, never a scripted workshop fixture or older model campaign checkpoint. Preserve all historical configurations and results.

Swap models by declaring their exact GGUF file digest, filename, observed API metadata and chat-template digests. The server API does not compute a weight-file hash; a separate verified launcher receipt establishes the local files and runtime actually launched.

Prompt preflight sends the exact generation body to the pinned server's non-generating input-token endpoint. Context, output and cumulative token allowances are separate from the 65536-byte serialized-payload ceiling. Require returned prompt usage to match the measured count; account unexpected returned usage before rejecting it.
Use only literal loopback transport, one loaded model and one isolated native runtime at a time. No hosted SDK, credential forwarding, hidden retry, automatic WAIT, chosen action or gameplay rescue.

Native parser, executor and documented factual action reference are unchanged. The typed decoding grammar explicitly requires DIG mode and three-entry integer rectangles; this is not a replacement native legality validator.
The longer segment scheduling allowance accounts for bounded identity/token checks as well as generation. The independent runtime deadline and teardown still apply.

This development condition changes model, transport, schema, sampling, context accounting, payload limit and scheduling relative to earlier Ollama experiments. Do not treat unlike short attempts as model rankings or causal ablations. Repeated matched campaigns remain required.
Zero metered model API charges do not imply zero hardware, electricity or existing-host costs. No claim of reconciled project spending is made.

This is a fresh long development campaign from the original save, not a resume with an enlarged historical budget. It changes dispatch, token and scheduling allowances and adds periodic sibling checkpoints within each single copied runtime. Intermediate checkpoints do not restart the game. A failed later decision still requires explicit reconciliation; an earlier checkpoint is not the latest state.

Stop before another decision if observed free space is below 1 GiB, and reject a native snapshot copy if its measured save bytes would cross that floor. These are observed-space guards, not a filesystem quota or a guarantee against other processes filling the disk. No historical artifact is deleted, migrated or overwritten.

This separately declared v2 changes only the generation read timeout from 180 to 600 seconds. The observed v1 request was canceled while still generating; one dispatched request has no returned usage. Its trace and forensic native save remain retained and are not a resumable checkpoint. Start v2 from the original digest-bound save, never the failed v1 state. The independent 7200-second segment deadline remains unchanged.
